question: What would you call the middle elongated part of the female reproductive part of a flower?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Style**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The female reproductive organ of a **flower** is known as the **carpel** or **pistil**, which consists of three distinct parts: the **stigma**, the **style**, and the **ovary**.
 
• The **Style** is the **middle elongated part** of the **carpel** that connects the **stigma** to the **ovary**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Style.***
 
• One of its primary **functions** is to act as a physical barrier or a selective track for the growth of the **pollen tube**, ensuring that only compatible **pollen** reaches the **ovules**.
 
• The **Style** serves as a support structure that elevates the **stigma** to a height where it is more likely to capture **pollen grains** from **pollinators** like insects, birds, or the wind.
 
• During the process of **fertilization**, after a **pollen grain** germinates on the **stigma**, the **pollen tube** must travel through the internal tissues of the **style** to reach the **female gametes** located in the **ovary**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stigma:**
 
 
• The **Stigma** is the **terminal** or topmost part of the **carpel**.
 
• Its main **feature** is a **sticky** or feathery surface designed to receive and trap **pollen grains** during **pollination**.
 
• It plays a crucial role in **pollen recognition**, where the plant determines if the **pollen** is from the same species and is suitable for germination.
 
 
 
• **Ovary:**
 
 
• The **Ovary** is the **basal swollen part** of the **pistil** situated at the bottom of the **style**.
 
• It contains **ovules**, which house the **egg cells**; after **fertilization**, the **ovules** develop into **seeds** and the **ovary** matures into a **fruit**.
 
• In **Angiosperms**, the **location** of the **ovary** can be **superior**, **inferior**, or **half-inferior** depending on its position relative to other floral parts.
 
 
 
• **Pollen Grain:**
 
 
• A **Pollen grain** is not part of the female reproductive system; rather, it is the **male gametophyte** of **seed plants**.
 
• It is produced within the **anther** of the **stamen** (the male reproductive part).
 
• It contains **generative cells** that eventually produce **male gametes** required for **sexual reproduction** in plants.
 
 
 
• **Pistil vs. Carpel:**
 
 
• A **carpel** is the basic unit of the **gynoecium**. A **pistil** may consist of a single **carpel** (**simple pistil**) or several **fused carpels** (**compound pistil**).
 
• The **Gynoecium** is the collective term for all the female parts of a **flower**.
